findings.description: The guard is meant to skip the theme reset only when testSelectBottomPlacement is skipped on iPad. Because it uses `name.contains("testSelectBottomPlacement") || iPad()`, the reset is skipped for every OnboardingTests test on iPad. On iPad, testFirstRunTourDarkMode calls switchThemeToDarkOrLight("Dark"), and teardown no longer switches back to Light. The iPhone run of testSelectBottomPlacement, which finishes onboarding, also loses the reset that the base code did. Fix: use `&&`.
findings.failureMode: Dark theme is left applied after tests run on iPad, and iPhone testSelectBottomPlacement skips cleanup. This leaks state into later tests.
findings.title: `||` skips the theme reset for every iPad test and for iPhone testSelectBottomPlacement

findings.description: XCTest only runs methods whose names start with `test`. After the rename to `verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders`, test case C2864380 no longer runs in any plan and gives no warning. The AccessibilityTestPlan skip entry `testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders()` now points at a method that no longer exists. Fix: keep the `test` prefix, and skip the test explicitly in the plans if that is the intent.
findings.failureMode: The test silently stops running, so a regression in Bookmarks→Share→Reminders is not detected.
findings.title: Renaming the test to `verify…` stops XCTest from discovering it

findings.description: The new `return` leaves tearDown before `app.terminate()` and `try await super.tearDown()`. As a result, BaseTestCase/XCTestCase teardown never runs for the matching tests, and the app is left running. The base code always ran both calls. Fix: skip only the theme switch and let execution continue to terminate and super.tearDown.
findings.failureMode: Teardown chain is bypassed and the app is not terminated after the affected tests.
findings.title: Early `return` in tearDown skips app.terminate() and super.tearDown()

On case-sensitive filesystems (Linux/Docker/CI) loading members-api throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND, breaking members service boot.
findings.failureMode: Cannot find module '../../lib/magic-link/magic-link' at startup; members API fails to load.

Donation service init throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Fix: update the require in donation-service-wrapper.js to './donation-bookshelf-repository'.

findings.description: @Roles("TEAM_MEMBER") lets plain MEMBER users mint team invite links. The PR says TEAM_ADMIN is required, the tests expect a MEMBER to get 403, and the matching org controller uses TEAM_ADMIN. Fix: use @Roles("TEAM_ADMIN").

findings.title: createInvite returns identifier instead of token

findings.title: buildInviteLink condition inverted

findings.failureMode: Lint failure under --error-on-warnings.
findings.title: Unused GetUser import fails lint

findings.description: handleShowReaderModeAction changed `displayView: .readerMode` to `.readerModeLongPressAction`. BVC handles `.readerModeLongPressAction` by calling toggleReaderModeLongPressAction (add to reading list), so a plain tap on the reader-mode toolbar button no longer toggles reader mode and instead adds the page to the reading list. Restore `.readerMode`.
findings.failureMode: Tapping reader mode button adds to reading list instead of entering reader view.
findings.title: showReaderMode now maps to readerModeLongPressAction

findings.description: Base kept url only when `isWebPage() && !isReaderModeURL`; now `isWebPage() || isReaderModeURL`, so internal reader-mode URLs (localhost reader URLs) are passed to ToolbarAction.cancelEdit and shown in the address bar after cancelling edit (tabs/menu/cancel tap) instead of being cleared.
findings.failureMode: Address bar shows internal reader-mode URL after cancelling edit while in reader mode.
findings.title: cancelEditMode reader-mode URL check inverted (&& ! → ||)

findings.description: `case .available: true / default: false` flipped to `false / true`. Tapping when reader mode is available (about to enable) now reports disabled, and vice versa; the comment still says "will be enabled". Also changes the recorded extras in existing ToolbarMiddlewareTests reader-mode test.
findings.failureMode: Glean reader_mode_button_tapped records the opposite enabled state.
findings.title: Reader mode telemetry enabled flag inverted

findings.description: `private let gleanWrapper` became `let gleanWrapper`, exposing an implementation detail module-wide, violating AGENTS.md rule 11 (private for implementation details); nothing in the diff needs it.
findings.failureMode: Internal telemetry wrapper becomes externally accessible, violating access-control mandate.
findings.title: gleanWrapper access widened from private

findings.description: The diff deletes the unicode_escape conversion: `keyword_like_val = f"%{keyword[:30].encode('unicode_escape').decode('utf-8')}%".replace(r"\u", r"\\u")`. WorkflowRun.inputs and outputs are saved with json.dumps using the default ensure_ascii=True, so text like "中文" is stored as "\u4e2d\u6587". Searching for "中文" now uses the raw characters, which never match the stored text, so non-ASCII keyword searches return nothing. Fix: unicode-escape the keyword first, then apply escape_like_pattern.
findings.failureMode: Log search for Chinese or other non-ASCII keywords returns zero results
findings.title: Non-ASCII keyword search on workflow logs broken

findings.description: escape_like_pattern prefixes %, _ and \ with a backslash, but the SQL declares ESCAPE '|'. So "\" is taken as a literal character and "%" and "_" stay wildcards. For example, a search for "test_data" becomes '%test\_data%', which only matches text that contains a literal backslash. Queries that contain %, _ or \ return wrong or empty results. Fix: use ESCAPE '\'.
findings.failureMode: Full-text LIKE fallback returns no or wrong documents for queries containing _, % or \
findings.title: IRIS LIKE uses ESCAPE '|' but pattern escaped with backslash

findings.description: The value is backslash-escaped, but notlike() gets no escape="\\", unlike the like() calls next to it. The result then depends on the database's default LIKE escape. On a backend or SQL mode where backslash is not the default escape, "\%" is read as a literal backslash plus a wildcard, so the metadata filter excludes the wrong documents. Fix: pass escape="\\".
findings.failureMode: "not contains" metadata filter mismatches values containing %, _ or \ on dialects without backslash default escape
findings.title: "not contains" notlike missing escape clause

findings.description: `escapedPattern` is a camelCase local variable. AGENTS.md rule 16 requires snake_case for variables. Fix: rename it to escaped_pattern.
findings.failureMode: Repository naming mandate violated (rule 16)
findings.title: camelCase local variable violates snake_case mandate

findings.description: Removed `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL` from hashTypeSet in hincrbyfloatCommand. Master now clears field TTL on HINCRBYFLOAT while replica (HSETEX KEEPTTL) keeps it — reverse inconsistency, and a user-visible TTL loss on master (HINCRBY still keeps TTL).
findings.failureMode: HSETEX h1 EX 100 FIELDS 1 f1 1; HINCRBYFLOAT h1 f1 1.1; HTTL h1 FIELDS 1 f1 returns -1 on master (was ~100), replica still ~100.
findings.title: HINCRBYFLOAT drops HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL on master

findings.description: Helper used only in t_hash.c (no header declaration) had `static` removed, violating AGENTS.md rule 7 and exporting an internal symbol.
findings.failureMode: Internal helper becomes a global symbol, polluting namespace; violates mandatory static rule.
findings.title: addHashFieldToReply loses static

findings.description: `if rendered is not None and not isinstance(rendered, str)` lets a missing/None `result` through, and the method returns None although it's typed `-> str`. TemplateTransformNode._run then does `len(rendered)`, which raises an uncaught TypeError (only TemplateRenderError is caught), so the node crashes instead of returning a FAILED NodeRunResult. Trigger: an injected code_executor (DifyNodeFactory(code_executor=...)) whose response has no `result` key or a null one. Fix: raise TemplateRenderError whenever `not isinstance(rendered, str)`, including None.
findings.failureMode: Executor result lacking a string 'result' → render_template returns None → TypeError in node _run instead of a FAILED result.
findings.title: Renderer returns None despite str contract; node crashes on len(None)

findings.description: Pool moved to macOS-15 and displayName now says 'Use XCode 16.4.0', but the script still runs `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app/Contents/Developer` (lines 166 and 392). macOS-15 hosted images do not ship Xcode 15.2, so xcode-select errors with invalid developer directory and every macOS job fails at this step. Fix: point both scripts at /Applications/Xcode_16.4.0.app/Contents/Developer.
findings.failureMode: macOS CI jobs (public and internal) fail at the Xcode selection step.
findings.title: xcode-select still targets Xcode 15.2 on macOS-15 image

findings.description: Added `AND '$(AspNetCorePatchVersion)' == '1'` makes the BUILD002 "package references changed since last release" error fire only for 10.0.1 — the one patch whose baseline (Baseline.Designer.props still 9.0.0) is known stale — and silently disables it for 10.0.2 and every later servicing build. Condition appears inverted; should be `!= '1'` (or removed) so later servicing builds still enforce it.
findings.failureMode: In 10.0.2+ servicing builds, a removed package dependency (breaking servicing change) is no longer caught; in 10.0.1 the check runs against a 9.0.0 baseline.
findings.title: BUILD002 servicing check limited to patch 1 only

findings.description: The file-scoped `namespace ...ServerExecutionTests;` became a braced block namespace (closing brace at line 209), violating AGENTS.md rule 2 which requires file-scoped namespaces. Fix: revert to the file-scoped declaration and drop the added braces.
findings.failureMode: Mandatory repository convention violated on changed lines.
findings.title: File-scoped namespace replaced by block namespace

findings.description: `testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders` was renamed to `verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders`. XCTest only finds methods whose names start with `test`, so this case (TestRail 2864380) never runs again. AccessibilityTestPlan.xctestplan:371 still lists `ShareLongPressTests/testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders()`, and that entry now points to nothing. This also breaks AGENTS.md rule 6, which requires the `test` prefix. Fix: keep the `test` prefix. To stop running the test on purpose, use XCTSkip and say why.
findings.failureMode: Test coverage is lost without any error and a test plan entry is left stale.
findings.title: Renaming to verify* silently disables the Reminders bookmark test

findings.description: The comment says the theme is not changed on iPad, but testFirstRunTourDarkMode calls `switchThemeToDarkOrLight(theme: "Dark")` on every platform. With the new `|| iPad()` condition, the reset to Light is skipped on iPad. ClearProfile's resetApplication clears caches, cookies and documents but not UserDefaults, so the Dark theme can carry over to later tests on iPad. Fix: drop the `iPad()` condition from the theme-reset skip.
findings.failureMode: Dark theme state leaks into subsequent iPad tests.
findings.title: iPad no longer resets theme after testFirstRunTourDarkMode

findings.description: The new `return` inside the `#available` block leaves `tearDown` entirely. For every iPad test on iOS 17+, and for testSelectBottomPlacement on iPhone, `app.terminate()` and `try await super.tearDown()` (BaseTestCase and XCTestCase cleanup) no longer run. The app keeps running between tests and the base-class teardown is skipped. Fix: skip only the theme switch, for example `if !(cond) { switchThemeToDarkOrLight(...) }`, and still run terminate and super.tearDown.
findings.failureMode: Teardown cleanup chain is bypassed for iPad and testSelectBottomPlacement runs.
findings.title: Early return in tearDown skips app.terminate() and super.tearDown()

findings.description: @Roles("TEAM_MEMBER") lets any team member (MEMBER role) mint invite links; the intended/tested contract is TEAM_ADMIN (sibling org invite controller uses TEAM_ADMIN). Fix: @Roles("TEAM_ADMIN").
findings.failureMode: A MEMBER calls POST /v2/teams/:id/invite and gets 200 with a valid invite token — authorization bypass; e2e test expecting 403 fails.
findings.title: Invite endpoint allows plain team members

findings.description: `token: newToken.identifier` returns "invite-link-for-teamId-N" rather than the random token (base returned `token`). Affects trpc createInvite and both API v2 invite controllers. Fix: return `newToken.token`/`token`.
findings.failureMode: Callers receive a non-secret, constant identifier as the token; it doesn't match the link token and can't be used to join; repeated calls return identical "token".
findings.title: Returns identifier instead of token

findings.description: Base returned /teams link when `!isOrgContext`; now `if (isOrgContext)` returns /teams for orgs and /signup for regular teams. Fix: restore `!isOrgContext`.
findings.failureMode: Every invite link (trpc and API) points to the wrong flow: regular-team invitees sent to signup/getting-started, org invitees to /teams.
findings.title: Inverted org-context condition in buildInviteLink

findings.description: GetUser is imported but never used; biome lint --error-on-warnings (mandate 6) flags unused imports.
findings.failureMode: Pre-commit/lint with error-on-warnings fails on this file.
findings.title: Unused GetUser import fails lint

findings.description: `if rendered is not None and not isinstance(rendered, str)` lets None through, even though `render_template` is declared to return `str`. If an injected `code_executor` returns a mapping with no `result` key, or with `result: None`, the adapter returns None. `TemplateTransformNode._run` then calls `len(rendered)` outside the `TemplateRenderError` handler, so the node crashes with an uncaught TypeError instead of returning a FAILED result. Fix: use `if not isinstance(rendered, str): raise TemplateRenderError(...)`.
findings.failureMode: A None result from an injected executor raises an uncaught TypeError at len(rendered) instead of producing a controlled render failure.
findings.title: String guard lets a None render result through

findings.description: write_and_make_executable now returns Result<(), FileWriteError>, but prepare_tools (returns crate::Result) applies `?` to it at every call site. crate::Error (error.rs) only has #[from] for io::Error etc., no From<FileWriteError>, so tauri-bundler fails to compile on Linux (E0277). Also violates AGENTS.md rule 8 (manual Display/Error instead of thiserror).
findings.failureMode: Build failure of tauri-bundler on Linux targets.
findings.title: FileWriteError has no From into crate::Error; `?` fails to compile

findings.description: Order reversed vs base (`fs::write` then `set_permissions`). All callers invoke this only when the path does not exist, so set_permissions returns ENOENT and every tool download/inline write fails; even for existing files, fs::write keeps mode so result is fine but for new ones it errors. Fix: write first, then set permissions.
findings.failureMode: AppImage bundling on a fresh tools dir errors with 'Failed to set permissions: No such file or directory'.
findings.title: set_permissions before write fails on missing file

findings.description: Base was `if !gtk.exists()`. Now the inlined gtk plugin is written only if it already exists; on a fresh tools dir linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh is never created, yet linuxdeploy is always run with `--plugin gtk`. Fix: restore `!gtk.exists()`.
findings.failureMode: linuxdeploy fails to find the gtk plugin; AppImage bundling fails for new users.
findings.title: Inverted gtk.exists() check: plugin never written

findings.description: Base downloaded `linuxdeploy-{linuxdeploy_arch}.AppImage`; now `{arch}`. For i686 builds this requests linuxdeploy-i686.AppImage instead of the i383-named release asset used by base, so the download 404s (and local filename still uses linuxdeploy_arch). Fix: use `{linuxdeploy_arch}` in the URL.
findings.failureMode: i686 AppImage bundling fails with HTTP error downloading linuxdeploy.
findings.title: linuxdeploy URL uses arch instead of linuxdeploy_arch

findings.description: AGENTS.md rule 8 requires custom error enums to derive thiserror::Error; FileWriteError manually implements Display and Error. Fix: #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)] with #[error(...)] attributes.
findings.failureMode: Mandate violation; inconsistent error handling.
findings.title: Custom error enum hand-implements Display/Error (rule 8)

findings.description: The added `'$(AspNetCorePatchVersion)' == '1'` limits the servicing baseline error to the one patch where the baseline is known to be stale (Baseline.xml is 9.0.0, ValidateBaseline=false for 10.0.1). Directory.Build.targets.in uses `!= '1'` for the same patch-1 exemption. With `== '1'`, 10.0.1 servicing builds fail BUILD002 against the stale 9.0.0 baseline, and 10.0.2 onward silently skip the check.
findings.failureMode: 10.0.1 servicing build errors with BUILD002 for references removed since 9.0.0; 10.0.2+ skips the reference-removal check entirely.
findings.title: BUILD002 guard inverted: fires only in patch 1, disabled for later patches

It also no longer matches BrowserViewController's updated `@MainActor @Sendable` parameter, which receives this handler. Every other forwarder in this file keeps `@Sendable`. Under Swift 6, which this PR enables, the optional requirement can become a near-miss, or passing the non-Sendable closure to the `@Sendable` parameter can fail to compile. In the near-miss case, JS `alert()` panels are no longer routed through this delegate.
findings.failureMode: Swift 6 build error or near-miss witness: JS alert panels are not forwarded to BVC

findings.failureMode: Violates the access-control mandate.
findings.title: Internal-only helpers made public

findings.description: The new local SlotInfo declares fromUser.id: string, but the type it replaces (IGetAvailableSlots -> IFromUser) has id: number, and getUserAvailability fills it with user.id, which is a number. useAvailableSlots now returns this mistyped shape. BookerPlatformWrapper passes that schedule to the Booker, whose schedule prop uses useScheduleForEventReturnType with IFromUser { id: number }. As a result, either the types clash, or any atoms code that reads fromUser.id gets a string type while the runtime value is a number. Fix: declare id: number.
findings.failureMode: OOO slot payload has fromUser.id numeric (e.g. 1) but the type says string; the value is also incompatible with Booker's IFromUser{id:number} schedule prop.
findings.title: SlotInfo.fromUser.id typed string, runtime/source type is number

findings.description: The Slot type was moved out of trpc, which had userIds?: number[], and now declares userIds?: string[]. Slot user IDs are numbers everywhere else (TimeFrame.userIds: number[]). Code that uses the public onTimeslotsLoaded(slots: Record<string, Slot[]>) API will type numeric IDs as strings. Fix: keep number[].
findings.failureMode: A consumer that compares slot.userIds against string IDs, as the type tells it to, never matches the numeric runtime values.
findings.title: Slot.userIds changed from number[] to string[]

findings.description: validateCreateScheduleInput throws plain new Error(...), which breaks mandate #10 (typed error classes). It also checks only name and casts the rest (schedule, eventTypeId) without checking them, which bypasses the Zod schema pattern from mandate #5. The function is not called anywhere. Fix: validate with a Zod schema and throw a typed error.
findings.failureMode: Input like {name:"x", eventTypeId:"abc"} is returned as a valid CreateScheduleInput, and failures surface as untyped generic Errors.
findings.title: Hand-rolled validator throws generic Error and skips field validation

findings.description: Lines 40, 41 and 47 use single quotes ('object', 'Invalid input: ...', 'string'). biome.json sets quoteStyle to "double", so `biome format`/`biome check` flags this file and the formatting mandate (#3) fails.
findings.failureMode: The Biome format check reports a formatting diff on this new file.
findings.title: Single-quoted strings violate Biome double-quote formatting

findings.description: The removed line `config_metadata.inner = serde_json::from_value(value)...` was replaced with an insert into extensions only. The merged `value` is computed and then thrown away, so `--config` overrides passed to the Xcode/Android Studio scripts (xcode_script.rs:145, android_studio_script.rs:98) never take effect.
findings.failureMode: CLI --config overrides are silently ignored in mobile build scripts
findings.title: merge_with no longer applies merged config to inner

findings.description: An extension cannot be both "json" and "json5", so the condition is always false. Schema validation of tauri.conf.json/json5 never runs, and invalid configs no longer produce the error log and exit(1). Replaced line: `|| config_path.extension() == Some(OsStr::new("json5"))`.
findings.failureMode: Invalid configs pass silently without schema error reporting
findings.title: Schema validation condition changed from || to &&

findings.description: `config.get("bundle")` gives an object (or nothing), so `.as_str()` returns None. `original_identifier` is therefore always None, and mobile/mod.rs:395/412 fails with "app configuration is missing an identifier" when writing or reading the options server address file.
findings.failureMode: Every mobile dev/build fails with a missing-identifier error
findings.title: original_identifier reads "bundle" key instead of "identifier"

findings.description: The `let schema: JsonValue = serde_json::from_str(...).expect(...)` line is about 160 columns, which exceeds max_width=100. This breaks the mandated `cargo fmt --all -- --check`.
findings.failureMode: Format CI check fails
findings.title: Line exceeds rustfmt max_width; cargo fmt --check fails

findings.description: WorkflowRun.inputs/outputs are saved with json.dumps (ensure_ascii=True), so non-ASCII characters are stored as \uXXXX. The deleted line `keyword[:30].encode('unicode_escape')...replace(r"\u", r"\\u")` turned the keyword into that same escaped form. The new code matches the raw keyword instead, so a search for "你好" never matches stored "\u4f60\u597d". Fix: apply unicode_escape to the keyword before calling escape_like_pattern, which then escapes the resulting backslashes.
findings.failureMode: Keyword search in workflow logs returns no results for Chinese or other non-ASCII input/output text
findings.title: Dropped unicode_escape breaks non-ASCII keyword search

findings.description: escape_like_pattern prefixes %/_/\ with a backslash, but the SQL declares '|' as the escape character. So the backslashes are matched as literal text: searching "test_data" builds "%test\_data%", which only matches text that actually contains "test\_data". Searching "50%" still treats % as a wildcard. Fix: use ESCAPE '\'.
findings.failureMode: Full-text fallback returns no results for queries that contain _, % or \
findings.title: IRIS LIKE uses ESCAPE '|' but pattern escaped with backslash

findings.description: The value is backslash-escaped, but unlike the contains, start with and end with branches, this notlike call omits escape="\\". The result then depends on the database's default LIKE escape. For example, MySQL with NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES treats the backslashes literally, so "not contains 50%" excludes nothing it should. Fix: pass escape="\\".
findings.failureMode: Metadata "not contains" filter can return wrong documents when the value contains special characters
findings.title: "not contains" notlike missing escape clause

findings.description: The local variable `escapedPattern` is camelCase, which violates mandate 16 (snake_case for variables). Rename it to escaped_pattern.
findings.failureMode: Violates the repository's mandatory naming rule
findings.title: camelCase local variable violates snake_case mandate

findings.description: Loop uses `j <= keys_result->numkeys` (base: `j < numkeys`). Last iteration reads keys[numkeys] (stale/zero pos, e.g. argv[0] command name, or beyond heap keys array) and writes slot_buffer[numkeys], one past the malloc'd buffer. For a single-key GET in cluster mode, iteration j=1 hashes argv[0] ("GET") → different slot → CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT, so ordinary single-key commands are rejected with CROSSSLOT; plus heap overflow write / possible OOB argv read crash. Fix: `j < keys_result->numkeys`.
findings.failureMode: Heap buffer overflow and spurious CROSSSLOT errors for all keyed commands in cluster mode.
findings.title: Off-by-one loop reads/writes past keys and slot_buffer

findings.description: New slot_buffer uses malloc() and free() (lines 1110, 1120, 1124), violating AGENTS.md rule 2; allocation is untracked by used_memory and malloc's NULL return is unchecked (NULL deref on OOM, unlike zmalloc which panics cleanly). The buffer is never read, so it can be removed entirely; otherwise use zmalloc/zfree.
findings.failureMode: Untracked memory allocation, unchecked NULL on OOM; mandate violation.
findings.title: Direct malloc/free instead of zmalloc/zfree

findings.description: The rename changed `pageActionStack.arrangedSubviews` to `browserActionStack.arrangedSubviews`, so browser actions appear twice and the trailing page actions are left out. updateActionStack sets alpha=0 on newly added buttons, and the trailing stack's new buttons now never get reset to 1.0. Reload, share and reader mode stay invisible. Fix: use trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews.
findings.failureMode: Trailing page action buttons render invisible
findings.title: Trailing page action buttons stay invisible (alpha 0)

findings.description: The base anchored toolbar.leading to leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor; the new line anchors it to rightSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor. Together with toolbar.trailing == rightSkeleton.leading, this makes the toolbar's width equal to minus the right bar's width. That is unsatisfiable, so Auto Layout breaks constraints and the address toolbar lays out wrongly when swiping tabs is enabled. Fix: restore leftSkeletonAddressBar.
findings.failureMode: Conflicting constraints, broken toolbar layout
findings.title: Toolbar leading anchored to right skeleton bar

findings.description: The base code checked `pageActionStack` (the trailing stack); the new code checks leadingPageActionStack. The divider sits between locationView and the trailing page actions. When there are trailing actions but no leading ones, the divider now collapses to 0. When there are leading actions but no trailing ones, a divider is shown by mistake. Fix: check trailingPageActionStack.
findings.failureMode: Divider shown or hidden incorrectly
findings.title: Divider width now keyed on leading stack instead of trailing

findings.description: `isLandscape` is never read. The compiler warns that the value is unused, and the line calls the deprecated UIApplication.shared.statusBarOrientation, which is a lint and warning violation under the SwiftLint mandate. Fix: remove the line.
findings.failureMode: Compiler and lint warnings; dead code
findings.title: Unused isLandscape uses deprecated statusBarOrientation

findings.description: The leading anchor changed from `leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor` to `rightSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor`. The toolbar's trailing edge is also pinned to rightSkeleton.leading, so leading = right.trailing and trailing = right.leading give a negative width. With swiping tabs enabled, the constraints become unsatisfiable or produce a broken layout. Fix: restore leftSkeletonAddressBar.
findings.failureMode: Unsatisfiable Auto Layout constraints and a broken address toolbar layout when swiping tabs is enabled.
findings.title: Toolbar leading anchored to right skeleton

findings.description: The rename changed `pageActionStack.arrangedSubviews` into `browserActionStack.arrangedSubviews` (now listed twice), not `trailingPageActionStack`. New trailing page buttons get alpha 0 in updateActionStack and are never set back to 1, so reload/share/reader-mode buttons stay invisible.
findings.failureMode: Trailing page action buttons stay at alpha 0 and are invisible on the mainline toolbar configure path.
findings.title: Trailing page action buttons never faded in

findings.description: The base code checked `pageActionStack` (the trailing stack). The new code checks `leadingPageActionStack`. The divider sits between locationView and trailingPageActionStack, so with trailing actions and no leading actions it collapses to 0, and with leading actions only it shows a stray divider. Fix: use trailingPageActionStack.
findings.failureMode: The divider is missing when it should show and shows when it shouldn't, which gives a wrong address bar layout.
findings.title: Divider width keyed off wrong stack

findings.description: `isLandscape` is computed with the deprecated `UIApplication.shared.statusBarOrientation` but never used. This causes compiler warnings (unused value, deprecated API), and SwiftLint rules in the mandates may flag it. It is dead code with no layout effect.
findings.failureMode: Build and lint warnings from an unused variable and a deprecated API.
findings.title: Unused deprecated isLandscape variable

findings.description: `j <= keys_result->numkeys` does one extra pass. It reads keys[numkeys], which is a zeroed keysbuf entry (pos 0, meaning argv[0], the command name) or memory past the end of the zmalloc'd keys array when there are more than 6 keys. It also writes slot_buffer[numkeys], past the end of the malloc(numkeys) buffer. In cluster mode `GET foo` hashes "GET" against "foo", gets CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT, and preprocessCommand rejects essentially every keyed command. Large multi-key commands can crash on a garbage argv index. Fix: use `j < keys_result->numkeys`.
findings.failureMode: Heap overflow/OOB read; false CROSSSLOT for all keyed commands in cluster mode
findings.title: Off-by-one `<=` loop reads past keys and overflows slot_buffer

findings.description: slot_buffer is allocated with `malloc` (line 1110) and released with `free` (lines 1120, 1124), which violates AGENTS.md rule 2 (use zmalloc/zfree). The memory is not counted in used_memory, and the result is never NULL-checked before `slot_buffer[j]` is written. Fix: use zmalloc/zfree, or drop the buffer, since it is only written and never read.
findings.failureMode: Mandate violation; memory is not counted in used_memory; NULL deref on OOM
findings.title: Direct malloc/free violates zmalloc mandate

findings.description: Changes "strict": true to false, violating mandate 11 and removing strictNullChecks/noImplicitAny for all of src; `tsc -b --noEmit` validation no longer catches null/implicit-any errors (e.g. new field.value?.[0] typing).
findings.failureMode: Type-check enforcement weakened repo-wide; null/undefined bugs pass validate:types.
findings.title: TypeScript strict mode disabled

findings.description: Status is always bound to trigger.expect regardless of posture. With Proactive ("Stays in"), expect=[prefect.work-pool.ready] means "fire if Ready is NOT seen within N s", the opposite of staying in Ready. Deployment and flow-run fields switch to trigger.after for Proactive. Same defect in work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx line 36. Fix: name={posture === "Proactive" ? "trigger.after" : "trigger.expect"}.
findings.failureMode: Proactive work pool/queue automations fire on the wrong condition.
findings.title: Proactive "Stays in" writes status to expect, not after

findings.description: String.split("\n") always returns at least one element, so `lines.length > 0 ? lines : undefined` never yields undefined. Clearing the textarea stores expect=[""], and a trailing newline adds a "" entry. The trigger then expects an event named "", which never matches. Fix: filter out empty lines when building the value, and set undefined when none remain.
findings.failureMode: Custom automation expects the event "", so it never matches or fires as intended.
findings.title: Empty/blank lines become "" expected events

findings.description: parseInt truncates number-input values: "1e3" becomes 1, "2.5" becomes 2, and a cleared field gives NaN. The sibling components use Number(e.target.value). Fix: use Number(e.target.value).
findings.failureMode: Threshold value saved differs from what the user typed.
findings.title: Threshold parsed with parseInt, unlike other templates

findings.description: write_and_make_executable now returns Result<(), FileWriteError>, but callers in prepare_tools (-> crate::Result) use `?`. crate::Error has #[from] for io::Error/anyhow::Error but no From<FileWriteError>, and `?` does not chain conversions, so tauri-bundler fails to compile on Linux. Fix: keep io::Result or add a thiserror #[from] variant to crate::Error.
findings.failureMode: Compile error E0277 in tauri-bundler on Linux targets.
findings.title: FileWriteError has no From into crate::Error: build fails

findings.description: Order was swapped: base wrote then chmod'd. `fs::set_permissions` on a path that doesn't exist yet returns NotFound, and every caller only invokes this when `!path.exists()`, so every download/inline write of AppRun, linuxdeploy, gstreamer and appimage plugin fails. Fix: write first, then set permissions.
findings.failureMode: AppImage bundling errors with 'Failed to set permissions: No such file or directory' on any fresh tools directory.
findings.title: set_permissions before write fails on new files

findings.description: `if gtk.exists()` (base `if !gtk.exists()`) means on a fresh tools dir the inlined gtk plugin is never written, so `linuxdeploy --plugin gtk` can't find the plugin and AppImage bundling fails; when a stale file exists it's rewritten every run. Fix: `if !gtk.exists()`.
findings.failureMode: AppImage bundling fails on fresh machines/CI because linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh is missing.
findings.title: Inverted exists() check: gtk plugin never written

findings.description: Base downloaded `linuxdeploy-{linuxdeploy_arch}.AppImage`; the diff changes it to `{arch}`, so for i686 the downloaded asset name (`linuxdeploy-i686.AppImage`) no longer matches the mapped release name / cached filename (`linuxdeploy-i383`). i686 bundling fetches a different/non-existent asset. Fix: restore `{linuxdeploy_arch}`.
findings.failureMode: i686 AppImage builds fail to download linuxdeploy (404) or get a mismatched binary.
findings.title: linuxdeploy URL uses arch instead of linuxdeploy_arch

findings.description: The set_permissions line is 101 chars, above max_width=100; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` would rewrap it, violating AGENTS.md rule 3. Fix: run cargo fmt.
findings.failureMode: cargo fmt --check CI failure.
findings.title: Line exceeds rustfmt max_width, fails fmt check

findings.description: AGENTS.md rule 8 requires custom error enums to use #[derive(thiserror::Error)]; FileWriteError hand-writes Display and Error impls. Fix: derive thiserror::Error with #[error(...)] attributes.
findings.failureMode: Mandate violation (rule 8) on new error type.
findings.title: Custom error manually implements Display/Error, not thiserror

findings.description: rewriteClientCommandVector is given argc=6 but seven objects (HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field value). Only the first 6 va_args are read, so newobj is dropped and the propagated command is `HSETEX h1 KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 f1` with no value. Replicas and AOF reload reject it (wrong number of args/syntax error), so the increment is never applied there and master/replica/AOF diverge. Fix: pass 7.
findings.failureMode: Every HINCRBYFLOAT propagates a malformed HSETEX; replica/AOF lose the write.
findings.title: argc 6 drops value from HSETEX rewrite

findings.description: Base called hashTypeSet(..., HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE | HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL); the diff removes HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL. HINCRBYFLOAT on a field with a TTL now clears the TTL on the master, while the replica applies HSETEX KEEPTTL and keeps it — the inconsistency is inverted rather than fixed, and field TTLs are silently lost. Fix: restore HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL.
findings.failureMode: HSETEX h1 EX 100 FIELDS 1 f1 1; HINCRBYFLOAT h1 f1 1.1 → HTTL on master returns -1 instead of ~100.
findings.title: HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL dropped on master

findings.description: The diff removes `static` from addHashFieldToReply, which is only used within t_hash.c (grep). This violates AGENTS.md rule 7 (internal helpers must be static) and exports an unneeded symbol with no prototype. Fix: restore `static`.
findings.failureMode: Needless global symbol; mandate violation, possible -Wmissing-prototypes warning.
findings.title: addHashFieldToReply lost static

findings.description: The diff changes `"strict": true` to `"strict": false` in the app tsconfig, so validate:types stops checking null/undefined and implicit any across ui-v2/src. That breaks mandate 11 and weakens the CI type-check gate. Fix: restore `"strict": true`.
findings.failureMode: Type errors such as unchecked nulls pass validate:types in CI and ship.
findings.title: Strict type checking disabled for the app

findings.description: `"".split("\n")` returns `[""]`, so `lines.length > 0` is always true and the `undefined` branch never runs. When the user clears the textarea, expect becomes `[""]` instead of being empty. On the backend, an empty expect means "any event", but `[""]` fails `matches` for every event. The trigger then never matches. Fix: set undefined when the text is empty, e.g. `e.target.value === "" ? undefined : lines`.
findings.failureMode: A custom automation saved with a cleared events box has expect [""], so the reactive trigger never fires.
findings.title: Cleared custom events become [""], which matches no events

findings.description: Every other threshold input, including flow-run-state and the other three new components, uses `Number(e.target.value)`. Here it is `parseInt(e.target.value)`. When the field is cleared, parseInt('') returns NaN where Number gives 0. Input like '1e2' becomes 1 instead of 100. The NaN or truncated value gets stored as trigger.threshold. Fix: use Number(e.target.value).
findings.failureMode: Clearing the Threshold field stores NaN in trigger.threshold, and the input then shows NaN or an empty value.
findings.title: Work-pool threshold uses parseInt instead of Number

findings.description: handleShowReaderModeAction changed `displayView: .readerMode` to `.readerModeLongPressAction`. BVC handleDisplayActions maps `.readerMode` to toggleReaderMode() and `.readerModeLongPressAction` to toggleReaderModeLongPressAction() (add to reading list). Tapping the toolbar reader mode button (or accessibility magic tap / summarizer long press) now adds the page to the reading list instead of entering/exiting reader mode; `.readerMode` becomes unreachable. Restore `.readerMode`.
findings.failureMode: Reader mode button no longer toggles reader mode; instead adds page to reading list.
findings.title: showReaderMode now maps to readerModeLongPressAction

findings.description: Condition changed from `(currentURL.isWebPage() && !currentURL.isReaderModeURL)` to `(currentURL.isWebPage() || currentURL.isReaderModeURL)`. Reader-mode URLs (http://localhost:port/reader-mode/page?url=...) are web pages, so base excluded them; now when the user cancels editing (tabs/menu/cancel button) while on a reader-mode page, the internal localhost reader URL is dispatched in ToolbarAction.cancelEdit and shown in the address bar instead of being cleared. Restore `&& !isReaderModeURL`.
findings.failureMode: Internal reader-mode localhost URL leaks into address bar after cancel edit.
findings.title: cancelEditMode now keeps reader-mode URLs

findings.description: recordReaderModeTelemetry flipped `case .available: true / default: false` to `false / true`. Tapping when reader mode is `.available` (i.e., enabling it) now records enabled=false, and tapping while active records true. Also breaks the existing testDidTapButton_tapOnReaderModeButton_dispatchesShowReaderModes (nil state → default → true, which flows into the swapped isPrivate extra, failing `XCTAssertEqual(savedExtras.isPrivate, false)`). Restore the original mapping.
findings.failureMode: Wrong telemetry for every reader-mode tap; existing unit test fails.
findings.title: Reader mode telemetry `enabled` value inverted

findings.description: `private let gleanWrapper` became `let gleanWrapper` (implicit internal) with no external user (grep finds none). Violates AGENTS.md rule 11 requiring private for implementation details; exposes the wrapper so callers can bypass the typed telemetry API. Restore `private`.
findings.failureMode: Access control rule violation; implementation detail exposed module-wide.
findings.title: gleanWrapper loosened from private to internal

findings.description: Diff deletes `struct UX { static let buttonSize: CGFloat = 40 }` and replaces `UX.buttonSize` with literal `40` in the closeButton height/width constraints, violating AGENTS.md rule 13 (UI constants must live in a nested UX struct). Fix: restore the UX.buttonSize constant (private) and use it.
findings.failureMode: Mandate violation: button size becomes a duplicated magic literal scattered in layout code; changing it requires editing two literals and the UX namespace no longer documents it.
findings.title: UX constant replaced by magic number 40

findings.description: `if rendered is not None and not isinstance(rendered, str)` lets None through, even though `render_template` is declared to return `str`. If an injected `code_executor` returns a mapping with no `result` key, or with `result: None`, the adapter returns None. `TemplateTransformNode._run` then calls `len(rendered)` outside the `TemplateRenderError` handler, so the node crashes with an uncaught TypeError instead of returning a FAILED result. Fix: use `if not isinstance(rendered, str): raise TemplateRenderError(...)`.
findings.failureMode: A None result from an injected executor raises an uncaught TypeError at len(rendered) instead of producing a controlled render failure.
findings.title: String guard lets a None render result through
